title: improv·artist · tender (Felix Gonzalez-Torres)
mutation_directive: improv artist: tender via Felix Gonzalez-Torres

improv_extras.practice: candy spills, light strings, paired clocks; intimacy as sculpture

v1.feedback: The Gonzalez-Torres reference lands well — the warm amber incandescent palette on an L-system armature genuinely reads as light-string drape, and the fallen-particle candy-spill on the ground plane is a thoughtful second layer from the artist's practice. The catenary sag and slow breathing sway earn their compute without being noisy. Two things to tighten: the 80k particle count feels over-budget for what's essentially a branching wireframe with glow — halving count and increasing per-bulb size would push closer to the chunky, physical warmth of actual Gonzalez-Torres light strings rather than a diffuse shimmer. The fall cycle is a nice idea but at 30s it's too slow to notice on first viewing; shortening to ~12s with a more visible detach moment (brief brightness pulse as a particle releases) would make the 'tender loss' reading land faster.

v2.feedback: The light-string catenaries and candy-spill pool are direct, legible Gonzalez-Torres references — good. But the L-system tree armature reads more Christmas-tree-with-lights than intimate gallery corner; Gonzalez-Torres draped bare bulbs wall-to-wall in empty rooms, so the organic branching fights the tenderness rather than supporting it. Reduce branch particle budget (25% is too much visual weight on scaffolding), let the catenary strings span open space without a visible support tree, and cluster the candy pile tighter beneath — right now the 1.5–3.5 unit scatter is too diffuse to read as the slow, grieving accumulation the spills evoke.
